title: Non-local Stabilization and Synchronization of Larmor Precession in Trapped Polariton Condensate Dimer
authors: Stepan Baryshev, Alexey Yulin, Ivan Gnusov, Sergey Alyatkin, Pavlos G. Lagoudakis
abstract: We demonstrate mutual synchronization of Larmor precessions between spatially separated, optically trapped polariton condensates. We identify the cross-condensate correlation g(2)1,2(τ) as a sensitive metric for condensate coupling. Synchronization of precessions in a condensate dimer is mediated by polariton outflow and resonantly depends on spectral overlap and precession winding. All-optical stirring of one site non-locally increases the pseudo-spin dephasing time of its static neighbor, prolonging phase-locking in a dimer by an order of magnitude. Our work establishes a scalable platform for studying non-equilibrium time-periodically driven systems and for high-speed spinoptronic networks.
summary: The authors demonstrate that Larmor precession in two coupled polariton condensates can become mutually synchronized, even when only one condensate is actively driven. By measuring cross-correlation functions, they show that driving one site non-locally stabilizes the coherence of its neighbor, creating a robust, tunable platform for studying quantum synchronization in solid-state systems.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate and characterize the mutual synchronization of Larmor precessions between two spatially separated, optically trapped polariton condensates.
main_result: Optical stirring of one condensate non-locally stabilizes and prolongs the pseudo-spin dephasing time of its neighbor by an order of magnitude, establishing a master-slave entrainment mechanism.
method: The study uses polarization-resolved Hanbury-Brown-Twiss interferometry to measure second-order intensity correlation functions, $g^{(2)}_{1,2}(	au)$, which serve as diagnostics for condensate coupling and synchronization.
model_or_system: The physical system is a polariton condensate dimer formed in a microcavity, exhibiting spinor degrees of freedom that undergo Larmor precession due to intrinsic energy splitting. The coupling is mediated by polariton outflow between the two sites.
key_observables: Cross-condensate correlation function $g^{(2)}_{1,2}(	au)$, pseudo-spin dephasing time, and the spectral overlap/winding direction of the precessing pseudo-spins.
important_parameters: Spectral overlap, precession winding direction, and the strength of the optical stirring field relative to the Larmor frequency.
main_assumptions: The coupling mechanism is assumed to be mediated by polariton outflow, and the analysis often relies on approximations like the Kuramoto model or weak fluctuation limits.
figures_summary: Figures show $g^{(2)}_{i,i}(	au)$ curves comparing static vs. stirred traps to demonstrate dephasing time prolongation, and $g^{(2)}_{1,2}(	au)$ dependence on separation and spectral detuning to map out synchronization regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from demonstrating basic synchronization via correlation functions to quantifying the non-local stabilization effect using optical stirring, and further explores the underlying physics by analyzing polarization plane locking using advanced correlation measurements.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental platform to study non-equilibrium, time-periodically driven quantum systems, offering insights into collective dynamics and entanglement-like phenomena (master-slave coupling) in strongly interacting bosonic systems.
